text: End of course test, Track 2. I love it when the power stops working. Why? Well, it gives me a chance to see the night sky, something that fewer and fewer people see these days. Hi everyone, and welcome to this week's podcast. I'm talking about a threat you might not know about. Light pollution. That is, the light from street lights and houses that stop us from seeing the beautiful night sky. The light bulb is one of the greatest things ever invented. We all agree on that. Can you imagine what life would be like without them? By turning on a light switch, we have the power to turn the dark into light. But this also causes problems. More than 80% of the world's population lives under skies that are polluted by light. To put it another way, over 6 billion people live with light pollution. In some places that have a lot of light pollution, like Singapore, there is so much light that you can only see 0.05% of the stars in the sky. About 14% of the world's population don't even use their ability to see at night. Some cities, like Las Vegas, are so bright that you can see their lights from over 65 km away. Light pollution might not be as serious as other issues, but it does cause problems for the environment. It is bad for animals, like birds, that move a lot at night, because it can make them go the wrong way. Studies show that light pollution affects other species that don't even live in the cities. These include bats, fish, turtles and monkeys. Every year, millions of baby sea turtles die, because the lights make them confused and they can't find the ocean where they would be safe from other animals. Light pollution also damages human health. It doesn't matter if it's a computer screen or a street light shining through a window. Too much light affects the natural light-dark cycle of day and night and upsets our biological clock. In other words, we don't know when to sleep and when to wake up. This can damage our health by increasing the risk of heart disease, obesity and cancer. It can also damage our mental health. When we don't sleep well, we get stressed. So, what can we do to keep healthy? We can't escape light pollution, but let me tell you a secret that may help a little. Looking at the clear night sky is very relaxing. It makes you feel like you are part of something bigger. Well, that's it for today. Tune in next time when I'll be talking about you.
